# Fulfilment Status Chip

## Summary
The one place the fulfilment blocks decide how a lifecycle hue renders: fill, border and text are all mixed `in oklch` from a single hue toward the theme's own tokens, so the chip stays legible on light and dark grounds and the three can never come apart.

## API
- `StatusChip` — template-only component; args `@label`, `@hue` (any CSS colour; the option tables pass hex), optional `@size` (`'small' | 'base'`)
- `StatusStyle` — `{ value, label, hue }`, the option-table row shape `Order Status` and `Shipment Status` export for each value

## Usage
```ts
import { StatusChip } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/fulfilment/fulfilment-status-chip';
import { orderStatusStyle } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/fulfilment/order-status';

{{#let (orderStatusStyle @model.status) as |style|}}
  <StatusChip @label={{style.label}} @hue={{style.hue}} />
{{/let}}
```

## Non-goals
Not a status field: it renders a hue it is handed. Vocabularies and transitions live in the status fields that consume it.

This chip is internal to the fulfilment cluster: its vocabularies (`Order Status`, `Shipment Status`) carry literal hex hues, which is what it accepts. For new work use the catalog `Status` field (`fields/status`) with `StatePill` (`components/state-pill`) — they take a named hue vocabulary and do the contrast-checked mixing. Converging the fulfilment vocabularies onto them is tracked separately.
